segments.t: Laura is afraid of hurting her mother by saying no, so the agents talk of a trick: be impossible, like a difficult star, so that the director refuses you. Now it's Nathalie's audition. Hervé fusses over Solveig with a long list of drinks, and she only wants water. We follow Nathalie. Here's the scene in French first; it's fine to catch just the feeling.
Non, merci. Un verre d'eau.
Non, Nathalie, tu ne peux pas faire ça.
Bien sûr que oui.
Tu ne sais même pas comment faire.
Qu'est-ce que tu en sais, Mathias?
C'est très poétique. Je suis très émue.
Bon, j'y vais.
Mais c'est toi qui veux partir.
Pars, alors! Pars!
Je ne suis pas surprise.
Tu as toujours aimé le vent.
Tu peux réessayer, sans tant de tragédie?
Quelque chose de plus neutre.
Si c'est ce que tu veux.
Depuis que tu es petite, je le savais.
C'est plus neutre?
Let's go through it. Solveig turns down coffee, tea and juice, and asks for the simplest thing there is.
Non, merci. Un verre d'eau.
'No, thank you. A glass of water.' The little word in the middle means 'of', just like a glass of water in English. Meanwhile Mathias whispers to Nathalie.
Non, Nathalie, tu ne peux pas faire ça.
'No, Nathalie, you can't do that.' He uses the casual 'you'; they've worked together for years. He has guessed her plan: to spoil the audition on purpose.
Bien sûr que oui.
'Of course I can.' Literally 'of course that yes'. A very French way to insist.
Tu ne sais même pas comment faire.
'You don't even know how to do it.' The word for 'even' slips in after the negative. Mathias means she is too good an actress to act badly.
Qu'est-ce que tu en sais, Mathias?
'What do you know about it, Mathias?' The tiny word before the action word means 'about it'. She is a little offended.
C'est très poétique. Je suis très émue.
'It's very poetic. I'm very moved.' The word for 'moved' ends in the feminine spelling because Nathalie is a woman, though it sounds the same. She is talking about the script, and she means it.
Bon, j'y vais.
'Right, here I go.' Literally 'I go there'. People say it before jumping into anything.
Mais c'est toi qui veux partir.
'But you're the one who wants to leave.' Now she is reading the script: a mother talking to her daughter. The pattern 'it's you who' puts the weight on the person.
Pars, alors! Pars!
'Go, then! Go!' Nathalie gives a casual command from the action word 'to leave'. Commands are our language point: the action word alone, with no word for 'you'. She plays it with huge drama.
Je ne suis pas surprise.
'I'm not surprised.' The two-part negative around the action word 'to be'.
Tu as toujours aimé le vent.
'You've always loved the wind.' The word for 'always' sits between the two parts of the past action word. Solveig listens, and then asks for something else.
Tu peux réessayer, sans tant de tragédie?
'Can you try again, without so much tragedy?' The verb for 'try again' is just 'try' with a prefix meaning 'again'. Solveig wants less drama.
Quelque chose de plus neutre.
'Something more neutral.' After the word for 'something', French adds a small linking word before the adjective.
Si c'est ce que tu veux.
'If that's what you want.' Nathalie starts again, in exactly the same tragic voice.
Depuis que tu es petite, je le savais.
'Since you were little, I knew it.' The word for 'since' starts the sentence, and the second verb is in the tense for long, ongoing things in the past.
C'est plus neutre?
'Is that more neutral?' Asked with total innocence. It wasn't neutral at all, and everyone in the room knows it. Now the whole audition again.
Non, merci. Un verre d'eau.
Non, Nathalie, tu ne peux pas faire ça.
Bien sûr que oui.
Tu ne sais même pas comment faire.
Qu'est-ce que tu en sais, Mathias?
C'est très poétique. Je suis très émue.
Bon, j'y vais.
Mais c'est toi qui veux partir.
Pars, alors! Pars!
Je ne suis pas surprise.
Tu as toujours aimé le vent.
Tu peux réessayer, sans tant de tragédie?
Quelque chose de plus neutre.
Si c'est ce que tu veux.
Depuis que tu es petite, je le savais.
C'est plus neutre?
Nathalie can't act badly even when she tries, and you followed a whole audition in French. See you next time!
Au revoir!
